title: Billing metering compliance: audit logs, retention policy, and SOC evidence for usage accounting
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Provide auditable, tamper-evident logs and retention controls for all billing/metering events (rate-limit decisions, quota enforcement, token usage, embedding/rep request counts) to satisfy SOC-type evidence requests and internal compliance. Scope covers: metering event production, ingestion pipeline, persisted audit store, access controls for auditors, retention/long-term storage, reconciliation evidence for billing disputes, and operational runbooks. Out of scope: wholesale redesign of rate-limiter architecture; incremental changes to existing rate-limiter to emit richer events are in-scope.
acceptance_criteria: All metering-related events are emitted with consistent schema including event_id, customer_id, route, model_version, tokens_charged, timestamp, enforcement_outcome
Audit store retains immutable copies for 7 years in WORM-enabled S3 bucket with write-once lifecycle and signed checksums
Access controls: auditors can obtain read-only exports via the Console export flow; exported evidence includes signed manifest and hash chain
Mapping doc that ties log artefacts to SOC control objectives (e.g., CC3.1, CC4.2) published to Confluence
Reconciliation report job available: daily invoice-vs-metering delta < 0.1% for top 90% customers by spend
Security review completed and any high findings remediated prior to release
comments: 2026-02-11 - Maya Chen: Kicked off discovery; interviewed billing, infra, and compliance. Key ask: immutable evidence for at least 5 years, preferred 7. Compliance wants mapping to SOC controls and an auditor-friendly export flow.

2026-02-18 - Lucas Patel: Spike complete. Proposed approach: add event enrichment in metering-producer (<-> rate-limiter) to include canonical event_id and signed HMAC over payload before sending to Kafka. Downstream, ingestion job writes to primary OLTP store (for live queries) and to audit-worm-bucket as NDJSON with signed manifest. Trade-off: small increase in write amplification and storage cost; mitigated by compression and tiered retention.

2026-02-24 - Security review (in-flight): Initial threat model shows risk around S3 object ACLs and signer key protection. Action: generate per-environment signing keys in KMS with restricted IAM roles. Security requested proof-of-rotations policy.

2026-03-01 - PM review (Anika Rao): Requested explicit handling for disputes — ensure raw events for a disputed invoice can be exported as a single bundle with checksums and human-readable mapping to invoice line items. Also request a customer opt-out policy for debug traces that contain PII.

2026-03-05 - Eng sync notes: Implementation plan split into three deliverables: (A) Event schema & producer changes, (B) Ingestion + WORM storage + manifests, (C) Console export UI + audit access. Blocker: lifecycle policy requires infra ticket for S3 retention tool (ENG-3984).

2026-03-09 - Lucas Patel: PR for producer changes created (see GitHub PR link). Unit tests cover schema validation and HMAC generation. Integration tests pending; setting up test harness against dev WORM bucket.

2026-03-10 - Compliance (J. Morales): Reviewed mapping doc draft; suggested adding examples for rate-limit edge cases (e.g., transient backpressure, burst enforcement). Assigned follow-up to include 3 sample dispute narratives.
2026-03-10 - Maya Chen: Marking security_review_required=true; scheduled security re-review for 2026-03-20 after key rotation policy is added.
